findings.title: Delete action never renders in the new alert list because it is still gated on rulerRule
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu now computes `canDelete` from both the ruler rule and the new Grafana prom-rule abilities (line 87), and the new list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2`) passes only `promRule`, never `rulerRule`. But the Delete item is still rendered behind `canDelete && rulerRule && ...`, so with `rulerRule === undefined` the Delete entry is never shown even when the prom-rule ability grants delete. This drops rule deletion from the alert list, which the previous `GrafanaRuleLoader` supported by loading the ruler rule. The `onClick` also passes `rulerRule` to `handleDelete`, so the `(rule: RulerRuleDTO, groupIdentifier)` handler contract has to be relaxed; the delete modal already only needs the `identifier` computed two lines above. Note the updated `GrafanaGroupLoader` test asserts exactly 4 menu items, so it codifies the regression instead of catching it.

findings.title: Silence notifications menu item is a no-op in the new rule list view
findings.body: In the list view `RuleActionsButtons.V2` receives only `promRule`, so `rule` (the `RulerRuleDTO`) is `undefined`. The menu still shows "Silence notifications" because `AlertRuleMenu` derives `canSilence` from the new Grafana prom-rule ability, and `handleSilence` just sets `showSilenceDrawer = true`. However the drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, which is never the case when `rule` is undefined, so clicking the menu item opens nothing. Either `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` must be refactored to accept the prom rule/identifier, or the Silence item must be hidden when no ruler rule is available. The new `GrafanaGroupLoader` test only checks that the item exists and never clicks it, so this is not covered.

findings.title: Grafana rules are rendered without a React key in the filtered list
findings.body: The `grafana` branch returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem ...>` without the `key` that the other branches pass (and that the old `GrafanaRuleLoader` element received from this map). The list is built incrementally with `rules.concat(...)` during infinite scrolling, so React will reconcile all items by position, emit "each child in a list should have a unique key" warnings, and can attach state belonging to one rule (open dropdown, delete modal, clone redirect inside `RuleActionsButtons`) to a different rule as pages are appended. Pass `key={key}` as in the `datasource` and default branches.

findings.title: Prom-rule abilities wrongly treat recording rules as not exportable/pausable
findings.body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` gates `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently` on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, whereas the ruler-based implementation that it mirrors used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` (i.e. alerting *and* recording rules). Grafana recording rules can be paused and exported today, so in the new prom-rule-driven list view the Export menu item disappears for Grafana recording rules, and a recording rule in the recently-deleted view would lose `DeletePermanently`/`Restore`. Only `Silence` should be restricted to alerting rules; the remaining actions should use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`.

findings.title: Federated rule-group detection removed from the shared ruler abilities hook
findings.body: The refactor replaced `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` with `const isFederated = false;` in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`. That hook is still reached via `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` from `RuleActionsButtons`/`RuleDetails`, whose `CombinedRule` still carries `rule.group.source_tenants`. As a result, Mimir federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable: Edit/Pause/Delete/Permanently-delete actions will be offered for groups the ruler API exposes as read-only, and the requests will fail. The federation flag needs to be threaded through (from the group or an extended group identifier) instead of being hard-coded to false.
